newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich urges Clinton to drop highway toll plan.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich urges Clinton to drop highway toll plan.

text.p: Republican House Speaker Newt Gingrich Friday urged President Clinton to withdraw a proposal to let states charge tolls on federal highways if they pledge to spend the revenue on the upkeep of roads.

"Now this is double taxation. Every time you buy gasoline, don't you pay a gasoline tax? Didn't the Clinton-Gore administration and the Democrats raise the gasoline tax in 1993?" Gingrich said in a speech to the National Federation of Republican Women.
"So I would call on the president to withdraw this proposal for a toll road. It is wrong," Gingrich said.
Clinton made the proposal Wednesday as part of a $174 billion six-year highway construction program.

The legislation would increase core highway spending by 30 percent. It seeks increased spending for auto safety, environmental cleanup, new transportation technology and helping people move from welfare to work.
